key_facts: 70-year-old man
Medical history of atrial fibrillation
Sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker placement
Prostate cancer treated with radiation and hormonal therapy
Obstructive sleep apnea
Left-sided Bell's palsy
Tobacco misuse
Preexisting left-sided incomplete facial nerve palsy

Severe photosensitivity

Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI
Left pleural effusion on CT thorax

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of headache and diplopia with cranial nerve palsies, irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type on biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening, mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT thorax

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI, cranial nerve palsies

shortlist.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Medical history of prostate cancer, mass-like thickening of the posterior left pleura on CT thorax

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type on biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening, irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of right-sided temporal headache, diplopia, and cranial nerve palsies, combined with imaging findings of irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus and systemic lymphadenopathy, is highly suggestive of lymphoma. The biopsy of the posterior left pleural thickening showing CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: While Tolosa-Hunt syndrome can cause similar symptoms, the presence of systemic lymphadenopathy and pleural effusion is not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus meningioma
rejected.why: Meningioma would not typically cause systemic lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion, and the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
rejected.why: The patient's prostate cancer was treated with radiation and hormonal therapy, and the biopsy results do not show evidence of prostate cancer metastasis.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus lymphoma
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, the presence of systemic lymphadenopathy and pleural effusion suggests a more widespread disease process, making 'Lymphoma' a more comprehensive diagnosis.

gold: CD5+ Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma presenting as Cavernous Sinus Syndrome
